For an established tyre specialist in Zaventem with a strong reputation in the automotive sector, we are looking for a Tyre Fitter.
 

You will join a family-oriented company where quality, customer service and teamwork are key priorities. Together with your colleagues, you will ensure that customers can get back on the road safely and with confidence.
 

What will your responsibilities as a Tyre Fitter include?
 
 

• Fitting and removing tyres on passenger cars and light commercial vehicles. 

• Balancing tyres and ensuring correct installation. 

• Assisting with tyre repairs. 

• Working with professional tools and modern equipment. 

• Keeping the workshop clean, tidy and well-organised. 

• Providing support where needed and helping your colleagues to ensure the smooth running of daily operations. 
 

• You have a passion for cars and an interest in mechanics. 

• You have technical insight and work accurately. 

• Experience as a tyre fitter or assistant tyre fitter is an advantage, but not essential. 

• You are eager to learn and open to developing new skills. 

• You enjoy hands-on work and take initiative by identifying tasks that need to be done. 

• You treat colleagues, customers and equipment with respect. 

• You can work both independently and as part of a team. 

• You are willing to work on Saturdays. In return, you receive a day off during the week. 

• You are fluent in English.

Our client is an International Banking Institution with an established presence in Belgium.To strengthen its Compliance team in Antwerp, the organization is currently looking for a Compliance Officer who will support the Head of Compliance and AMLCO across a broad range of regulatory and financial crime compliance responsibilities.

Jobomschrijving

• Support the Compliance Manager in the execution and monitoring of the annual compliance plan
• Contribute to the review and implementation of AML/KYC policies, procedures and transaction monitoring processes
• Ensure timely and accurate preparation of regulatory reporting and returns
• Perform ongoing transaction monitoring and escalate relevant alerts and findings to the AMLCO
• Provide compliance advice to the business regarding customer onboarding, KYC reviews, transactions and risk classifications
• Review name screening alerts, sanctions and potential matches identified during customer onboarding and periodic reviews
• Support compliance matters related to corporate banking, credit facilities, syndicated lending and correspondent banking
• Perform compliance reviews and testing in accordance with the Compliance Monitoring Plan
• Contribute to the periodic review of transaction monitoring parameters and controls
• Support the assessment and review of client, country and business-related compliance risks
• Perform data quality controls across the different compliance tools and systems
• Contribute to the Enterprise-Wide Risk Assessment and other compliance-related projects

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Law, Finance, Economics or another relevant field
• Minimum 2 years of relevant experience within Compliance in the financial sector
• Good understanding of AML/KYC, Customer Due Diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions and embargoes
• Previous experience within banking or another regulated financial institution is a strong advantage
• A financial crime or compliance certification is considered an asset
• Strong analytical skills with attention to detail
• Ability to work independently while collaborating effectively with different stakeholders
• Pragmatic, proactive and solution-oriented mindset
• Strong knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, PowerPoint and Word
• Very good command of English is required, Dutch is a plus

Waiter / Floor Supervisor – Brusketta Antwerp
 

Brusketta is a vibrant Neapolitan restaurant located on Jan van Rijswijcklaan in Antwerp. Known for its lively atmosphere, authentic Italian hospitality and busy services, we are looking for an e
xperienced Waiter / Floor Supervisor who is ready to take responsibility on the floor.
 

We are looking for someone who doesn't just serve tables, but takes ownership of the entire guest experience. Someone who leads by example, stays organized under pressure and knows how to keep a busy restaurant running smoothly.
Extra perk: 
Sundays off – every single week! Enjoy your Sundays with family and friends. No Sunday shifts at Brusketta!
 

What you’ll do
 
 

• Welcome guests, take orders accurately and advise on dishes and wines 

• Serve efficiently, even when the restaurant and terrace are full 

• Lead the floor during service: divide tasks, keep the pace and motivate the team 

• Keep communication between floor, bar and kitchen clear 

• Solve problems calmly before guests notice them 

• Make sure service standards and opening/closing routines are followed  

Who you are
 
 

• Experience as a waiter or shift leader in hospitality 

• A strong service mindset with natural leadership qualities 

• Energized by a busy restaurant, organized and hands-on 

• English and Dutch required; Italian or French is a plus  

What we offer
 
 

• A dynamic, energetic working environment. 

• Full-time contract, 38 hours per week 

• Competitive salary of €16–€18 gross per hour, negotiable depending on experience. 

• Holiday pay and year-end bonus in accordance with sector regulations. 

• Commuting and laundry allowances according to applicable conditions. 

• Career development opportunities within a growing restaurant group.  

Ready to take the lead?
 

Are you an experienced hospitality professional who enjoys the energy of a busy restaurant and knows how to bring out the best in a team?
 

We would love to meet you!
 

Join Brusketta and become the driving force behind our service!
 

Send your CV, a photo and a short introduction to 
hr@lvpgroup.be.

Start your career in Pharma in a Lab Support role!
 

Are you ready to make a real impact in the world of biotechnology? 
 

 
 

Are you detail-oriented and comfortable working in a rapid changing, clean environment with very strict procedures? Do you want to contribute to the production of innovative, life-saving cell therapies? Then this could be the opportunity for you.
 

After extensive training in aseptic working and Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP), you’ll join our Operations Team and support the production of the Carvykti treatment in a highly controlled cleanroom environment.
 

What You’ll Do
 

 
• Support the daily aseptic and manual production process, following strict procedures and quality standards.
 
• Prepare workstations, equipment, tools and materials for production.
 
• Clean and disinfect materials and equipment to maintain a sterile environment.
 
• Inspect equipment and ensure the correct transfer of materials between production zones.
 
• Work closely with operators and team leads to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality therapies to patients. 
 

Good to Know You’ll work in a sterile environment wearing protective clothing. This role follows a shift schedule including weekends. Full training is provided.

We are looking for you if:
 

 
• You live near Gent/Zwijnaarde or have reliable transportation such as bike or Car.
 
• Fluent in English, you thrive in teamwork and are eager to learn new skills.
 
• You are accountable and motivated to make a difference in patient's lives. 
 
• Your attention to detail is unmatched.
 
• Bonus points for familiarity with GMP standards, aseptic techniques, sterilization methods, and MS Office.

This position is part of our talent pool. We are not actively recruiting for this position at the moment, but we will carefully keep track of your application and contact you when the role becomes available again.
 

We are looking for experienced pharmaceutical professionals who want to actively contribute to the future of medicine. This is more than just a job, it is an opportunity to further develop your expertise and grow your career in a dynamic, mission-driven environment focused on patient impact.
 

If you already have experience in cleanroom operations, pharmaceutical manufacturing or chemical processes, or if you combine a relevant educational background with hands-on experience, we would very much like to hear from you.
 

Your role and responsibilities;
 
 
 
• Actively participate in aseptic and manual pharmaceutical manufacturing processes. 
 
• Work in cleanroom and laboratory environments in accordance with GMP standards. 
 
• Perform production activities in controlled environments (Grade A/B/C/D), including spiking, media exchanges, cell culture activities and freezing of therapeutic products. 
 
• Execute thorough cleaning and disinfection of materials and equipment. 
 
• Support transitions between production zones, ensuring compliance and continuity. 
 
 

This role is suited for you if you:
 

 
• Have relevant pharmaceutical experience or a Bachelor’s degree in Life Sciences.
 
• Have experience in a cleanroom, pharmaceutical, or chemical environment.
 
• Enjoy working in a structured environment and following procedures.
 
• Communicate fluently in English.
 
• Live near Zwijnaarde and can commute independently to the site.

As a Production Team Lead, you will be responsible for the daily production of personalized cell therapies for both clinical and commercial use in a sterile cGMP environment. You will coordinate the different units within the CAR-T process and ensure that all activities are carried out safely and in full compliance with cGMP requirements — while steering and organizing the operations from your office-based workspace, keeping a strong overview of the production flow and acting as the central point of coordination for the team. If you don't have prior leadership experience yet, that is also okay. 
 

What you can expect: 
 

 
• Coordinate and supervise operational units within the CAR-T manufacturing process, including component preparation, production support, CAR-T processing, filling & finishing, and cryopreservation.
 
• Act as the first point of contact for production issues and collaborate closely with Manufacturing Operations, QC IPC, Quality, Facilities & Engineering, MS&T/Manufacturing Excellence, Training, Planning, and Supply Chain.
 
• Serve as a domain expert for Quality and Operations in cGMP environments and play a key role during GMP inspections and external audits.
 
• Manage all quality-related production aspects, including procedures, work instructions, logbooks, transfer forms, batch record review and release, and overall cGMP compliance.
 
• Coordinate quality system activities such as Change Controls, Deviations/Events, and CAPA.
 
• Ensure proper training of team members and promote a culture of continuous learning.
 
• Drive operational excellence by initiating improvements that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance overall quality. 

Who we are looking for: 
 

 
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Science, Bio-Engineering, Pharmacy, or a related field, or equivalent through experience.
 
• Minimum 3 years of experience in a GMP environment, preferably in biotech or biopharma. 
 
• Experience in people management, or with relatable coordinating activities such as training, coaching, ... .
 
• Solid knowledge of cGMP regulations and cleanroom operations; familiarity with Microsoft Office is required, and experience with MES/EBR is a plus.
 
• Strong communication and organizational skills. You don’t need formal leadership experience, but you do show natural leadership qualities.
 
• Positive, flexible, and capable of prioritizing, multitasking, and solving problems effectively, with strong attention to detail.
 
• Fluent in English; additional languages are a plus.

This position is part of our talent pool. We are not actively recruiting for this position at the moment, but we will carefully keep track of your application and contact you when the role becomes available again.
 

Are you a (recent) graduate with a bachelor’s degree in biotechnology, chemistry, agro- or life sciences? Are you ready to put your knowledge and skills into practice in a setting where innovation meets purpose?
 

We’re looking for ambitious, detail-oriented professionals to help shape the future of medicine. At our leading biotech company, you won’t just find a job you’ll begin a meaningful, long-term career in advanced biomanufacturing.
 

Your journey starts with comprehensive training, where you’ll learn the fundamentals of aseptic (germ-free) techniques and GMP (Good Manufacturing Practice), the key standards that guide our industry. You’ll quickly gain confidence with the tools, procedures, and mindset that define high-quality biotech production.
 

After onboarding, you’ll join our dynamic Operations team, working hands-on with cutting-edge technologies and sterile processes. Together with your colleagues, you’ll perform precise manual and aseptic production steps, always following clear protocols to guarantee patient safety and product quality.
 

What your day-to-day will look like:
 

 
• Contributing to aseptic and manual production processes
 
• Working in a cleanroom laboratory environment
 
• Performing production steps in controlled areas (grade A/B/C/D), such as spiking, media changes, cell culture, and freezing therapeutic products
 
• Managing equipment, including inspections and maintenance
 
• Thorough cleaning and disinfection of materials
 
• Supporting transitions between production zones
 
• Ensuring patients receive high-quality therapies on time 

 
• You’re eager to apply your scientific background and contribute to something meaningful, making a real difference in the lives of patients.
 
• You’re energized by dynamic environments and excited to keep learning and growing within advanced biomanufacturing.
 
• You hold a bachelor’s degree in biotechnology, chemistry, agro- or life sciences, and you’re ready to take the next step from the classroom to cutting-edge industry.
 
• You value structure and precision, and you feel comfortable working in a sterile (aseptic) setting, wearing the proper cleanroom gear.
 
• High-tech equipment and innovative processes spark your curiosity, you want to be part of what’s next.
 
• You communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken.
 
• You’re a real team player with a strong eye for detail, and you understand the importance of following procedures carefully.
 
• You’re flexible and open to working in shifts.
 
• You’re excited about a 4-days-on, 4-days-off schedule that supports both focus and work-life balance.

As a Production Supervisor, you are responsible for the daily production process of personalized cell therapy, both for clinical and commercial purposes. You will lead various units within the CAR-T process and ensure safe and compliant production activities in accordance with cGMP requirements — all while coordinating and overseeing operations from your dedicated office workspace, maintaining a clear overview of the production floor and ensuring smooth cross-team collaboration.
 

Tasks:
 

 
• Lead and supervise operational units within the CAR-T production process, including component preparation, production support, CAR-T processing, filling & finishing, and cryopreservation.
 
• Act as the primary point of contact for production-related topics, ensuring smooth coordination with Manufacturing Operations, QC IPC, Quality, Facilities & Engineering, MS&T/Manufacturing Excellence, Training, Planning, and Supply Chain.
 
• Provide hands-on leadership on the shop floor, supporting teams in daily operations, troubleshooting, and decision-making in cGMP environments.
 
• Serve as a subject matter expert for Quality and Operations and play a key role during GMP inspections and external audits.
 
• Oversee production quality activities, including documentation management (procedures, work instructions, logs, transfer forms), batch record review and release, and compliance with cGMP standards.
 
• Coordinate quality system processes such as Change Controls, Deviations/Events, and CAPA.
 
• Guide and support team development through structured training and operational coaching.
 
• Drive operational excellence by leading process improvements focused on efficiency, cost reduction, and quality enhancement. 

Who we are looking for: 
 

 
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Science, Bio-Engineering, Pharmacy, or a related field, or equivalent through experience.
 
• Minimum 3 years of experience in a production environment, preferably in biotech or biopharma.
 
• Strong experience in management, for example as a production lead, supervisor, or similar leadership role.
 
• Solid knowledge of cGMP regulations, cleanroom operations, and familiarity with Microsoft Office; experience with MES/EBR systems is a plus.
 
• Strong communication, organizational, and leadership skills with an empathetic and people-oriented management style.
 
• Positive, flexible, and capable of prioritizing, multitasking, and solving problems effectively, with a strong attention to detail.
 
• Fluent in English (additional languages are a plus).

Processing incoming invoices and credit notes in accordance with internal procedures

• 
Managing invoice approval workflows

Monitoring outstanding vendor items

•

We are looking for an enthusiastic and reliable colleague who works accurately, takes initiative and enjoys contributing to a team.

You bring:

• 
Flexibility, reliability and a strong sense of teamwork

Knowledge of VAT legislation is considered an advantage. Previous experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central and Rydoo is also an asset.
